title: AIREP profile: evaluator_signature (independent evaluator attestation) v0.1
description: Validates a 'profiles.evaluator_signature' block: a THIRD signature role, distinct from the two the format already has. The core's integrity.signature is the PRODUCER's signature over the record content ('I made this record'); profiles.chain_witness carries a WITNESS signature over the chain head ('this is the current, untruncated head'). Neither says an independent party EVALUATED the decision. This profile carries an EVALUATOR's signed attestation: a party that re-checked the record's claim against its evidence and reached its own verdict, signing over the record's integrity.current with a key DISTINCT from the producer's. CRITICAL HONESTY: an evaluator signature made with the producer's own key is not an independent attestation — it only re-states the producer. A verifier MUST establish that evaluator_key_id differs from the producer's key (profiles.key_trust.key_id); a bare distinct evaluator_id string is not proof of a distinct key. This profile records the attestation and binds it to the exact record; it does NOT prove the evaluator performed a competent evaluation, only that a distinct key attested one. It attaches only under profiles.evaluator_signature and never changes the core: deleting the profiles block leaves a valid core record (the neutrality test).

evaluator_id.description: Identifier of the evaluating party (an organization, team, or individual). Unauthenticated text unless corroborated by the evaluator's key trust; the load-bearing identity is evaluator_key_id, not this label.

evaluator_key_id.description: Stable key id (kid) of the key that produced this attestation's signature. It MUST differ from the producer's signing key (profiles.key_trust.key_id) for the attestation to be independent — the whole point of a third signature. A verifier that cannot establish this distinctness cannot report the attestation as independent.

signed_over.description: The record's integrity.current that this attestation covers. Binding to integrity.current (not to a re-derived hash the evaluator computed for itself) is what ties the verdict to the exact content the producer signed. A verifier MUST check signed_over == the record's integrity.current; a mismatch means the evaluator signed a different record than the one presented.

verdict.description: The evaluator's own assessment of the record's claim against its evidence. 'concur' — the evaluator reached the same conclusion. 'dissent' — the evaluator disagrees with the producer's claim or decision. 'inconclusive' — the evaluator could not determine the claim from the evidence available to it. 'concur' is an independent second opinion, NOT a proof of correctness.

evaluated_at.description: When the evaluation was made (RFC 3339, UTC). An evaluation timestamp earlier than the record's own subject.timestamp_utc is a contradiction a reader should notice.

scope.description: What the evaluator actually checked, and what it did not — kept separate so a reader does not read a bounded evaluation as a total one.

covers.description: The specific propositions the evaluator assessed (e.g. 'the cited policy artifact resolves and matches its digest').

does_not_cover.description: What the evaluator explicitly did not assess (e.g. 'the factual correctness of the model output').

algorithm.description: The signature algorithm (for example 'Ed25519'), so a verifier can select the right verification routine.

public_key.description: Optional: the evaluator's public key (or a pointer) a verifier uses to re-check 'signature'. When absent, the verifier must resolve evaluator_key_id through an out-of-band trust store.

value.description: Key material in the named format, or a pointer when format is 'ref'.

signature.description: The evaluator's signature over the canonical form of {evaluator_id, evaluator_key_id, signed_over, verdict, evaluated_at}. A verifier that does not re-check this value has confirmed only that an attestation is PRESENT, not that it is valid.
